border.note: Alpha rather than solid so one token works over any surface.

bg-hover.note: The only hover treatment in the system.

scrim.note: Dims SoundCloud behind a dialog (the Go to URL prompt, the "not responding" dialog). Always paired with the Overlay shadow. Settings, a page, takes none.

title.purpose: A Settings section's title. The largest text in the entire product.

body.purpose: Setting names — the primary reading size in the panel.

label.purpose: Navigation items, inputs and selects. The dense working tier.

explanation.purpose: What a setting does, under its name in every Settings row and under each search match. 13px at line-height 1.45, at most 70ch, Muted Ink: read, not glanced at.

caption.purpose: When a setting takes effect, status lines and launch notices, the version and links at the foot of the Settings sidebar, and the window title in the chrome strip.

overline.purpose: One use only: the NOT IMPLEMENTED YET badge on a pending setting.

shadows.name: overlay
shadows.purpose: The only shadow in the system. A wide ambient layer plus a tight contact layer, used only when a surface floats above the app and takes over input: paired with the scrim on dialogs, alone on the context menu. Settings and the page-status surface stand in for the page and take none.

motion.name: dialog-enter
motion.purpose: A dialog (the Go to URL prompt, the "not responding" dialog): 14px upward fly plus fade, with the scrim fading over the same duration.

motion.name: settings-page
motion.purpose: Settings, a page rather than a dialog, fades in and out as a whole. No fly: nothing floats, so nothing rises.

motion.name: reduced-motion
motion.purpose: Under prefers-reduced-motion: reduce the duration collapses to zero rather than substituting a different animation.

motion.name: hover
motion.purpose: Hover states are instant. The wash appears on the frame it is needed; no transition.

breakpoints.name: window-min
breakpoints.purpose: Minimum window width enforced by BaseWindow; the chrome is not designed below it.

narrative.overview:
BetterSoundCloud is a frame around someone else's picture. SoundCloud's own web app renders every piece of music UI — the player, the waveforms, the artwork, the navigation — inside a content view that this design system deliberately never touches. What we own is a 32px strip along the top, a settings page that stands in for SoundCloud's below it, and future overlays. That is the entire canvas, and the frame's job is to hold the picture without competing with it.

This produces a system that is almost aggressively restrained. There is no display type, no hero, no imagery, no gradient, and no decorative colour anywhere. Controls are transparent until you hover them. The largest text in the product is 15px, outside two named exceptions for content read at a distance: lyric lines, and the full-screen showcase. The accent appears only where something is focused, selected, or on. A user should be able to look at this app all day and never notice the chrome — and then find every control exactly where they left it the moment they reach for one.

The restraint is architectural before it is aesthetic. Our chrome lives outside SoundCloud's document precisely so their releases cannot break it, and that same separation is why the frame must not imitate their surface language: two competing music UIs stacked in one window would read as a skin, not a client. Depth follows the same logic — surfaces are flat and separated by hairline borders, and a shadow appears only when something floats above the app and takes over input.

- One 32px chrome strip; nothing else is permanently on screen - Flat at rest — borders separate, shadows signal modality - Two radii, two shadows, one type family, one accent - Controls invisible until hovered; icons are 15px stroked outlines - Every colour defined twice, light and dark, and never hard-coded outside the token file - Honesty rendered visually: unbuilt features appear disabled and labelled, never functional-looking

rules.name: The Borrowed Accent Rule
rules.body: The accent is SoundCloud's, not ours. It marks state — focused, selected, on — and never decorates. If orange appears somewhere that is not a state, remove it.

rules.name: The Two-Mode Rule
rules.body: Every colour exists twice and is consumed only through a --bsc-* custom property. A literal hex outside tokens.css is a bug: it will be correct in one mode and wrong in the other. The single sanctioned exception is #fff on the danger hover, which must stay white in both modes.

rules.name: The 15px Ceiling Rule
rules.body: Nothing in BetterSoundCloud's own UI is larger than 15px. The frame has no headlines because the frame has nothing to announce. If a surface seems to need display type, it probably belongs to SoundCloud's view, not ours.

rules.name: The Two Sentences Rule
rules.body: A setting's explanation is one or two short sentences, never a paragraph. When it takes effect is not part of it: that is the row's own Caption note. (The maintainer's, 2026-11-14.)

rules.name: The System Stack Rule
rules.body: No webfonts, ever. The chrome inherits the OS UI font so it belongs to the window; the CSP on every renderer blocks remote font loads regardless.

rules.name: The 32px Rule
rules.body: The chrome is 32px and never grows. Every new affordance either fits in that strip, moves into settings, or becomes an overlay. Growing the frame steals from the picture.

rules.name: The Modality Rule
rules.body: Shadow is not decoration and not hierarchy — it means "this has taken over input". A surface that does not block interaction does not get a shadow. If you reach for elevation to make something look important, use a border and a tonal step instead.

rules.name: The Transient Rule
rules.body: The scrim marks a dialog, something the user has to finish or cancel. A popup that any click closes — a menu — floats without one. If a surface needs a scrim to be understood, it is a dialog and should behave like one.

rules.name: The Two Radii Rule
rules.body: 6px for anything you interact with, 10px for anything that floats. A third radius is a new concept — justify it or drop it.

dos: Do consume colour through --bsc-* custom properties, so every surface works in both modes.
Do keep the accent to state only — focus rings and selection. Its rarity is what makes it legible.
Do separate surfaces with 1px Hairline borders and the single tonal step, not with shadow.
Do pair the scrim and the Overlay shadow whenever something takes over input, and use neither otherwise.

Do give every new control a visible focus state (2px --bsc-focus outline, outline-offset: -2px) and full keyboard operability — the product targets WCAG 2.2 AA for its own chrome, and a new view takes part in F6 by itself.
Do render an unbuilt capability as a disabled control with the NOT IMPLEMENTED YET badge rather than hiding it or letting it appear functional.
Do expose stable data-bsc-* attributes on themable regions, and treat tokens.css plus those attributes as the versioned public API for user themes.
donts: Don't target Svelte's generated hash classes (.s-050uw8y64xWw) from a theme. They change every build. That is what the data-bsc-* attributes exist for.
Don't build a generic Electron dashboard — Material-style cards, elevation for its own sake, an icon rail, dense chrome competing with the content it wraps. Confirmed anti-reference.

Don't adopt consumer music-app surface language — gradient heroes, artwork bleeding into blurred backgrounds, oversized transport controls. SoundCloud already renders all of that one layer below; duplicating it makes the client a skin. Confirmed anti-reference. The one exception is the user's to turn on: the Visualizer plugin, flat and in the showcase's own ink (above).

Don't use glassmorphism, backdrop blur, glow, or saturated gradients. They read as a theme rather than a tool and destroy legibility in a 32px strip. Confirmed anti-reference. One exception, the user's to choose: the Glass setting (Windows 11, off by default, kept by the maintainer 2026-11-11), which puts the whole window on a dark live blur, like a theme does. Our chrome on it stays flat: a plain dark fill on the bars, no blur or glow of its own, and dark ink whatever the Appearance.
Don't introduce a webfont. The CSP blocks remote loads, and the OS stack is the point.
Don't add a third radius, a second shadow, or a second accent without retiring one first.
Don't exceed 15px type in BetterSoundCloud's own UI, outside the Lyrics and Showcase Exceptions.
Don't grow the chrome past 32px. New affordances go into settings or an overlay.
Don't style SoundCloud's page from a component stylesheet. Page-level appearance is CSS-only through insertCSS, and no node may be added to their document.
